cosy-lesson.title: "You don't have a soul. You are a soul. You have a body.": C.S. Lewis

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Essence – the intrinsic, core nature or indispensable quality of a living being.

p.em: Example: Many spiritual teachers believe that kindness is the true essence of the human soul.

cosy-blockquote.p: Consciousness – the state of being awake, self-aware, and cognizant of one's own existence.

p.em: Example: The mystery of human consciousness continues to baffle materialist scientists.

cosy-blockquote.p: Materialism – the tendency to value physical comfort and possessions over spiritual or intellectual growth.

p.em: Example: Extreme materialism often leads to a sense of inner emptiness, regardless of physical wealth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Transcendent – beyond or above the limits of normal physical or sensory human experience.

p.em: Example: A near-death experience can provide a transcendent glimpse into life beyond the physical body.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spirituality – the quality of being concerned with the human spirit or soul as opposed to material things.

p.em: Example: Personal spirituality can provide a deep source of hope during intense life challenges.

cosy-blockquote.p: Incarnation – the physical embodiment of a spiritual being or abstract soul in a fleshly form.

p.em: Example: According to Lewis, the body is just a temporary incarnation of our eternal self.

cosy-blockquote.p: Perception – the way in which something is regarded, understood, or interpreted through the senses.

p.em: Example: Our limited physical perception makes it difficult to see the intangible aspects of reality.

cosy-blockquote.p: Existential – relating to human existence, purpose, and the conscious search for meaning.

p.em: Example: Realizing that you are a soul can trigger a profound existential shift in your priorities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intangible – incapable of being touched or physically grasped; lacking a physical presence.

p.em: Example: The most valuable elements of our identity, such as love and memories, are completely intangible.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ethereal – extremely delicate and light in a way that seems spiritual rather than physical.

p.em: Example: She felt a quiet, ethereal peace while contemplating the silent mystery of the night sky.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the true essence of who you are if we completely separate your mind from your physical body?
★ Philosophers demand that we reflect deeply on life. Is it essential that everyone cultivate inner freedom?

How does Lewis's quote challenge the popular scientific theory that human consciousness is just a chemical brain reaction?
★ Have you ever experienced a sudden, quiet shift in your consciousness while walking in nature?

Why does a society obsessed with materialism struggle so much to understand C.S. Lewis's philosophy?
★ Have you ever had to choose between pursuing high materialism and protecting your peace?

Can we experience a truly transcendent connection with someone without relying on physical proximity?
★ Have you ever felt a highly transcendent emotion while listening to an old song?

How does personal, individual spirituality help us cope with physical pain and aging?
★ Do you actively nurture your own spirituality, or do you prefer practical logic?

If the body is merely a temporary incarnation of the soul, why are we so terrified of physical aging?
★ Does viewing your body as a simple incarnation make you feel more relaxed about your appearance?

How does our perception of daily stress change when we view ourselves as eternal souls?
★ Has your perception of what is important in life shifted over the last five years?

How does realizing that "you are a soul" help resolve a deep existential crisis of purpose?
★ What is the most important existential question you have ever contemplated?

Why are the most profound aspects of our human self completely intangible and unmeasurable?
★ What is the most beautiful intangible gift someone has ever given you?

How does quiet meditation allow us to experience an ethereal connection with our inner self?
★ Have you ever sat in absolute silence to feel that calm, ethereal state of mind?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is a person closest to experiencing their true "soul"? Rank them from most spiritual to most material: - 🪐 Digital Transcendence Uploading your entire intangible consciousness into a digital, virtual sky, leaving all physical bodies behind. - 🌿 Solitary Contemplation Living in complete, silent isolation, contemplating the ethereal mystery of the universe without physical distractions. - 🏛️ Material Perfection Surrounding yourself with physical beauty, gourmet food, and absolute sensory comfort in a material paradise. - 🧬 Temporary Incarnation Constantly changing physical bodies, experiencing many different human and animal lives over centuries.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, advanced neuro-technology will make it possible to measure a person's essence with mathematical precision. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you want to live in a world where everyone knows your true inner nature?

Future social networks will completely eliminate physical photos, prioritizing our consciousness and thoughts instead. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you hope digital media will ever become a place for honest self-expression?

A future world with less work and more leisure will fully destroy human materialism, forcing people to focus on spiritual growth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you had unlimited free time, how would you nurture your mind?

Artificial intelligence will be able to show a deeper level of transcendent connection than humans ever can. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you ever seek comfort from an AI companion during a difficult time?

Global mindfulness programs will completely eliminate standard religions, replacing them with a shared, universal spirituality. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you were a global leader, would you encourage daily silent meditation in all schools?

In the coming decades, human cloning will provide us with a perfect incarnation for our digital memory files. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live forever if you could upload your memory into a clone body?

Future communication technology will allow us to share and feel each other's perception of reality directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear a device if it could transfer your feelings to a loved one?

In a highly artificial world, resolving existential questions will become our most valuable social activity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you feel you can be fully authentic in your current career or studies?

Future technology will find a way to stabilize and photograph our intangible feelings and dreams. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear a shirt that turns red when you are feeling anxious or angry?

A future society fully focused on logic will leave no room for the quiet, ethereal beauty of individual identity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you agree that we must take emotional and creative risks if we want to grow?

ul.li: Incorrect: You don't have a soul, you are a soul → Correct: You don't have a soul; you are a soul ((Avoid comma splices by using a semicolon or breaking into two sentences))
Incorrect: I am agree with C.S. Lewis → Correct: I agree with C.S. Lewis (('Agree' is a verb, not an adjective))
Incorrect: I am not believing in souls → Correct: I don't believe in souls ((State verbs are not used in continuous forms))
Incorrect: It depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Third person singular requires '-s'))
